newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher ahead of federal budget.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher ahead of federal budget.

text.p: Delhi shares ended higher on Thursday as speculators bought ahead of India's federal budget, brokers said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was scheduled to present the 1997/98 budget for the fiscal year beginning April 1 to parliament at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) on Friday.
Brokers said Delhi's benchmark stocks index closed 16.15 points, or nearly two percent higher, at 744.41.
They said domestic institutions -- which have stayed on the sidelines in recent trading sessions -- were also bidders.
"It was a pre-budget rally mainly attributed to sizeable buying by speculators on hopes of some reliefs likely to be proposed in tomorrow's budget," said S.C. Juneja at brokers Jaico Credit.

Some brokers said the rally was unexpected as India's annual Economic Survey released on Tuesday had stated that "tax deductions and exemptions cannot be a substitute for reforms of policy and procedures."
Cement maker ACC climbed 57 rupees to 1,439 despite a 12 percent increase in freight rates announced in the railway budget on Wednesday.
Reliance ended 4.70 rupees higher at 270.95, TISCO rose 5.60 rupees to 191 and Hindustan Lever jumped 30 rupees to 900.
